The held-lock run is described above. The scan test stays as a supplementary check for what a run cannot observe without a 30-minute wait or a failing start: the bound's value, the parse sitting under the lock, and the release in the finally. Its `rat-tail:` comment now says exactly that. In a probe I ran both new tests against the plan's \u00a75 draft, which passed both, and against two wrong mains. The swallowing one fails :361. The one whose start re-reads the snippet fails :347 with `start peertube-engine@7070`.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 1 (D20 int): taken. :91 asserts `type(port) is int`.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 2 (abnormal path in `main`): taken, by the same held-lock run (:353-362).\nShape RECOMMENDATION 2 (lock-before-stop by line number): taken. :349 now checks the order at runtime, as lock state sampled at the moment each systemctl child runs, and :361 checks a held lock leads to no stop.\n</findings_addressed>\n\n<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_26_zero_downtime_deploy_phase1.py:346 \u2014 in a real in-process run of `main` with a 7071 snippet, the first child process is exactly [\"sudo\",\"-n\",\"/usr/bin/systemctl\",\"stop\",\"peertube-engine@7071\"]; :347 \u2014 the last child is exactly [\"sudo\",\"-n\",\"/usr/bin/systemctl\",\"start\",\"peertube-engine@7071\"], although the fake rewrites the snippet to 7070 as soon as the stop has run; :348 \u2014 those are the only two systemctl calls</assertion>\n<expected>Under the \u00a75 draft, applied in memory in a probe, the calls were [stop peertube-engine@7071, merge-staging-db.py, recompute-popularity.py, build-ann-index.py --cpu, start peertube-engine@7071]. On today's code the test is red because `main` exits SystemExit(2) on the unknown --engine-upstream-snippet (:344).</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A start that re-resolves the unit from the snippet. In the probe the last call read `start peertube-engine@7070`, which fails :347. Today's `service_name=args.service_name` gives `stop peertube-engine`, which fails :346. A `.service` suffix or a reordered argv fails the exact list comparison.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_26_zero_downtime_deploy_phase1.py:88, :91 \u2014 every rejected plan or JSON case raises ValueError, and every accepted one returns exactly the int port; :105-:109 of the scan-free unit test \u2014 engine_instance_unit spells @7070/@7071 with no .service and refuses 7069/7072</assertion>\n<expected>7070 and 7071 as int for the accepted cases, ValueError for the rejected ones. Taking the lock after the stop also puts the stop in `calls`. A `main` that passes a literal 1800 instead of the constant keeps waiting, and _run_main's 10 s join fails with \"main still running after 10 s\" rather than hanging the suite.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_26_zero_downtime_deploy_phase1.py:349 \u2014 in the free-lock run, the deploy lock is held, as sampled by a fresh open+flock attempt at the moment each systemctl child runs, at both the stop and the start (`[True, True]`); :350 \u2014 it is free once `main` is done</assertion>\n<expected>[True, True], then free. The flock holder is a real second open file description in the test process. Nothing project-owned is replaced, and the module is loaded from its file.\n6. It collects \u2014 yes.     "step_7_implement:1": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py`\n- **Imports and constants.** Added `import fcntl` and `import re`. After the imports, added these module constants: `ENGINE_INSTANCE_BASE = \"peertube-engine\"`, `ENGINE_INSTANCE_PORTS = (7070, 7071)`, `DEPLOY_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 30 * 60`, `DEPLOY_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS = 5.0`, and the two snippet regexes `UPSTREAM_ANY_SERVER_RE` and `UPSTREAM_SERVER_LINE_RE`. These use the same rule as the bash `read_active_port`.\n- **`parse_args`.** Two new options after `--skip-systemctl`:\n  - `--engine-upstream-snippet`, default `None`.\n  - `--deploy-lock-file`, default `<repo>/engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock`, resolved. It is a different file from `--lock-file`.\n- **New helpers after `systemctl_cmd`.**\n  - `parse_upstream_snippet(path) -> int`: the file needs exactly one `server` line, and it must be `server 127.0.0.1:7070;` or `\u20267071;`. Anything else raises `ValueError`, and so does an unreadable or missing file. It reads bytes and splits on `\\n` only, so a CRLF snippet is rejected the way the bash grep rejects it. The plan's `read_text` would have translated the CRLF away and accepted it.\n  - `engine_instance_unit(port)`: returns `peertube-engine@<port>` with no `.service` suffix, only for 7070 and 7071. Any other port raises `ValueError`.\n  - `acquire_deploy_lock(lock_path, *, wait_seconds, poll_seconds=DEPLOY_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS)`: opens the file `O_RDONLY|O_CREAT` (root may own it as 0644) and tries a non-blocking `fcntl.flock` every `poll_seconds` until `wait_seconds` is used up. It returns the fd. On timeout it closes the fd and raises `RuntimeError`.\n  - `release_deploy_lock(fd)`: does nothing for `None`; otherwise it unlocks and closes the fd.\n- **`main()`, stop/start block.**\n  - `engine_unit` starts as `args.service_name` and `deploy_lock_fd` as `None`.\n  - When `--engine-upstream-snippet` is given and systemctl is not skipped, the worker first takes the deploy lock with `wait_seconds=DEPLOY_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`. Only then does it resolve the unit, once, as `engine_instance_unit(parse_upstream_snippet(Path(args.engine_upstream_snippet)))`, logs it, and stops it. A lock timeout or a bad snippet therefore raises before anything is stopped.\n  - The stop and the start both pass `service_name=engine_unit`.\n  - The outer `finally` now wraps the start in its own `try` whose `finally` calls `release_deploy_lock(deploy_lock_fd)`. The lock is held through merge, popularity and the ANN rebuild, and is released after the start even when the start raises.\n  - The existing `test_main_runs_similarity_stage_after_service_start` scan still finds exactly one `Try` whose `finalbody` contains the start.\n  - Without the flag, the commands are the same as before.\n\n### `tests/active/upstream_snippet_cases.json` (new)\nThe plan's \u00a77.1 case table as a JSON list of `{id, text, port}`, with `port: null` for a rejected snippet. Accepted: `active-7070`, `active-7071`, `tabs-no-final-newline`. Rejected: `foreign-port`, `foreign-host`, `two-servers`, `server-params`, `commented-out`, `crlf`, `empty`.\n\n### `tests/active/test_updater_worker.py`\nNot touched. The phase checkpoint covers the plan's \u00a77.3 additions, and this step asked for production code only. The existing tests in this file still match the new `main()` structure: the start is still inside the outer `finally`, and `run_similarity_stage` still comes after that `try`.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

Environment, from ValidateTests [\"tests/tmp/test_probe_26_p2.py\"] (first version). The test runs as uid 1000 under pixi python at /home/enduser/code/PeerTube-browser/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python. bash 5.3.9 is at /usr/bin/bash, and flock, grep, mktemp, awk, tr, sleep, date, cp, mv and chmod are in /usr/bin. Real curl, systemctl, logger and id are also in /usr/bin, and nginx is at /usr/sbin/nginx, so the stub bin/ has to come first on PATH (it does: PATH=tmp/bin:/usr/bin:/bin). When a Python stub is symlinked as bin/systemctl, its sys.argv[0] basename is \"systemctl\", printed as \"systemctl ['is-active', 'x']\". While this process holds fcntl.flock, a child's `exec 9>>lock; flock -n 9` printed rc=1, and rc=0 once the lock was released. Under umask 077, mktemp gave mode 600, and a mv over the snippet left 600, so the 0644 check is only satisfied by an explicit chmod.\n2. The harness against the plan's \u00a72/\u00a73 draft, copied verbatim into tests/tmp/probe_26_p2_draft/ (dry-run branch omitted), with SCRIPT_SRC/LIB_SRC repointed: 35 passed in 37.7 s wall.\n3. Mutants of that draft, each run against the checkpoint test named for it, ValidateTests [\"tests/tmp/test_probe_26_p2.py\"] (second version). All 10 were caught: stop @old before check_switched, a status-only 7079 check (fails post-switch-wrong-upstream), replace_file without chmod (failed with 0o100600), the MainPID read after the stop (cache not removed), no snippet restore on rollback (nginx-test-failed), an updater check for \"active\" only (activating), no foreign-listener check, a parser that drops the one-server-line count (two-servers printed (0, '7071')), a lock on a different file (lock-held case exit=0), and no ROLLBACK FAILED text.\n4. I have no Delete tool, so I emptied both probe files to a single comment. tests/tmp/test_probe_phase2_harness.py and tests/tmp/probe_phase2_harness.py still need deleting. Nothing in the checkpoint needed rewriting.\n8. Red, not green: yes. The final ValidateTests run printed \"35 failed\", exit status 1.\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. Without a script nothing can be measured, so this precondition is the honest red. Removing it would turn the refusal negatives vacuous until their controls fail.\n10. Where a row names a wrong implementation I did not run as a mutant (missing chmod \u2192 0600, lock fd opened before option parsing), it is marked as reasoning in the row, not as an observation.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:2": "<changes>\n### `engine/engine-upstream.sh` (new, sourced, never run)\nThe bash side of the upstream snippet. It defines `ENGINE_INSTANCE_BASE=peertube-engine`, `ENGINE_INSTANCE_PORTS=(7070 7071)`, `ENGINE_LISTENER_PORT=7079` and `UPSTREAM_SNIPPET` (`${PEERTUBE_ENGINE_UPSTREAM_SNIPPET:-/etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf}`; the env var is only for tests). Functions:\n- `engine_deploy_lock_path <repo>` prints `<repo>/engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock`.\n- `read_active_port <path>` prints 7070 or 7071. The file must have exactly one line starting with `server`, and that line must be `server 127.0.0.1:7070;` or `\u20267071;` (`[[:blank:]]` around it). Anything else returns non-zero: a missing or unreadable file, CRLF line endings, a foreign host or port, two servers, server parameters. This is the same rule as `parse_upstream_snippet` in `updater-worker.py`.\n- `other_instance_port` returns the other port of the pair.\n- `snippet_text <port>` prints the three-line snippet.\n- `replace_file <dest>` replaces a file atomically from stdin. It uses `mktemp` in the destination's directory under a dotted name that does not end in `.conf`, then `chmod 0644`, then `mv -f`, and removes the temp file if any step fails.\n\nThe plan's `ENGINE_LISTENER_CONF` and `engine_listener_text` are not added here: only the Phase 3 installer uses them, so they belong in that phase.\n\n### `scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh` (new)\nThe plan's \u00a73 script. Usage is the header comment block. Options are `--blue-green` (required; without it the script prints usage and exits 2 before anything else), `--timeout` (300), `--warmup` (0), `--drain` (30), `--dry-run` and `-h`. The repo root is found the same way as in `run-services.sh`. The script sources `engine/engine-upstream.sh`.\n\nOrder of a run:\n1. Root check through `id -u`, then the required commands (`flock`, `curl`, `systemctl`, `nginx`, `logger`).\n2. `exec 9>>` on the lock file, `chmod 0644` on it, then `flock -n 9` (refused if held).\n3. Refused if `peertube-updater.service` is active, activating, deactivating or reloading.\n4. Client preflight: refused if the Client unit exists without `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7079`. The unit path can be overridden with `PEERTUBE_CLIENT_UNIT_PATH`.\n5. `read_active_port`, refused if the snippet is invalid or missing.\n6. A leftover target instance that is not inactive is stopped.\n7. Refused if anything still answers on the target port.\n8. Start the target, then wait for readiness: every 2 s; 429 or no answer means not ready; a `failed` or `inactive` unit ends the wait at once. Then the optional warm-up and one more check.\n9. Copy the snippet to a `.bak` backup, then set `PHASE=switching`.\n10. Write the target snippet with `replace_file`, run `nginx -t`, then `systemctl reload nginx`.\n11. Probe 7079 up to 10 times, 1 s apart. It needs a 200 whose `X-Engine-Upstream` names the target. Then `PHASE=switched`.\n12. Record the old instance's `MainPID`, drain, stop the old instance, enable the new one and disable the old one.\n13. Remove `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` and its `-journal`, then exit 0.\n\nHow failures are handled:\n- One `rollback` function acts on the phase.\n  - `pre-switch`: stop the target.\n  - `switching`: restore the backup, run `nginx -t`, reload, stop the target.\n  - `switched`: log `post_switch_failure`, carry on, and exit 1 at the end.\n- If a step inside rollback fails, it logs `event=rollback_failed msg=\"ROLLBACK FAILED\" at=<step>` with the snippet and both unit states, and exits 1.\n- `INT` and `TERM` traps route to the same rollback.\n- `sleep`, `curl` and `logger` get `9>&-`, so no child keeps the lock open.\n- Every line is `deploy_id=<UTC>-<pid> event=\u2026 k=v`. It goes to stdout and to `logger -t peertube-engine-deploy`.\n- `--dry-run` prints the ports, the updater and Client preflight state, and the ordered actions. It takes no lock and changes nothing.\n\nWhere I departed from the plan's draft:\n- **Foreign listener.** It is a `refuse` (`port_in_use_by_foreign_process`) rather than a `rollback`, because nothing has been started at that point.\n- **`logger` failure.** If `logger` fails, the script prints a warning to stderr instead of `|| true`, so the failure is not swallowed.\n- **Lock file mode.** The lock file is set to `chmod 0644` after it is opened. Phase 1's updater opens it `O_RDONLY` as the service user, and a root umask of 077 would otherwise leave it at 0600 and lock the updater out.\n- **Not gated:** `--dry-run`, `--help` and the warm-up check are in the approved \u00a73 design and the requirements, but this checkpoint does not exercise them.\n\n### `.gitignore`\nUnder the local data patterns, added `engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock` with a one-line reason: the existing `*.db*` patterns do not match it.\n\n### `tests/active/test_deploy_bluegreen.py`\nNot touched. The phase checkpoint in `tests/tmp` carries every C1/C2 case. This step asked for production code only, so this is the same handling as Phase 1's `test_updater_worker.py`.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\ntests/tmp/test_probe_26_p2_impl.py: a throwaway probe. It loaded the checkpoint module by path and ran every one of its test bodies against the new script: 37 passed, and `/usr/bin/flock` exists. I have no delete tool, so its content is now a single comment line asking for the file to be deleted, like the earlier `tests/tmp/probe_26_p2_draft/` leftovers; it collects no tests.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

In every case `unit=/etc/systemd/system/peertube-engine@.service`, ExecStart ending `--host 127.0.0.1 --port %i`, a single `listen 127.0.0.1:7079`, and no write or mutating call. Rejected snippets and prod `--port 7070`: exit 1, with nothing written, no mutating call and host paths unchanged.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>Writing the single `peertube-engine.service` gives a `unit=` of that path and goes red at :191. Creating the snippet during the dry-run changes the snapshot and goes red at :203. Accepting `--port` in prod exits 0 and goes red at :235. A refusal that runs `systemctl stop` first goes red at :238.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_26_zero_downtime_deploy_phase3.py:268-280: exit 0; the `[dry-run]` events include stop and disable for peertube-engine@7070 and @7071, rm of the template, the listener and the snippet, and `nginx -t`, ordered instances < rm template < rm listener < rm snippet < nginx -t; snippet bytes, tree, host paths and stub mutations unchanged.</assertion>\n<expected>Exit 0.     "step_7_implement:3": "<changes>\n### `engine/install-engine-service.sh`\n- **Library and flags.** It now sources `engine/engine-upstream.sh` from its own directory. It adds the flags `HOST_SET` and `PORT_SET`, which the `--host` and `--port` cases set, and the constants `PROD_TEMPLATE_PATH` (`/etc/systemd/system/peertube-engine@.service`), `LEGACY_PROD_UNIT_PATH` (`/etc/systemd/system/peertube-engine.service`) and `PROD_READY_TIMEOUT=300`.\n- **Mode dispatch.** The entry point runs `install_engine_prod` for `--mode prod` and the unchanged `install_engine_service` for dev. The dev dry-run output is byte-for-byte the same as before. `--print-default-service-name` still prints `peertube-engine`.\n- **`engine_listener_text`.** Prints the 7079 listener. It includes the snippet by absolute path, and its one `server` block has:\n  - `listen 127.0.0.1:7079` only;\n  - `server_tokens off`;\n  - its own `access_log`;\n  - `client_max_body_size 2m`;\n  - `location /` with `proxy_pass http://peertube_engine`, `proxy_set_header Host $http_host` and `add_header X-Engine-Upstream $upstream_addr`;\n  - no keepalive.\n  This function lives in the installer, not the library, because the installer is its only user.\n- **`wait_http_200`.** A curl poll every 2 s until HTTP 200 or a timeout.\n- **`install_engine_prod`, refusals and checks:**\n  - It refuses a non-default `--service-name`, and `--host`/`--port` in any form, even `--port 7070`. Both exit 1.\n  - It checks for `server.py` and the venv python.\n  - Outside dry-run only, it requires root and the commands `systemctl`, `journalctl`, `nginx`, `flock` and `curl`.\n- **`install_engine_prod`, deploy lock.** Outside dry-run only, it takes the deploy lock with `exec 9>>`, sets the lock file to `chmod 0644` (as the deploy script does, so the updater can open it read-only), then runs `flock -n`.\n- **`install_engine_prod`, snippet.** It reads the snippet before writing anything:\n  - missing: port 7070, `snippet=new`;\n  - valid: its port is kept, `snippet=existing`;\n  - invalid: exit 1, and nothing is touched.\n- **`install_engine_prod`, dry-run.** It prints the header (`active_port=<p> snippet=new|existing`, `unit=<template>`, the snippet and listener paths, the legacy-migration flag and the plan), then the unit, snippet and listener previews, and writes nothing. The unit preview is today's unit except that it ends `--host 127.0.0.1 --port %i`. A warning goes to stderr when `peertube-engine.service.d/` drop-ins exist.\n- **`install_engine_prod`, real install:**\n  1. Write the snippet (only if it is new), then the listener, then the template; `daemon-reload`.\n  2. Migrate the legacy unit if it exists: stop, disable, rm, daemon-reload, reset-failed.\n  3. Bring up the instance the snippet names: restart it under `--force`, start it if it is not active, and otherwise leave it alone. The port never changes.\n  4. Stop the other instance if it is running, disable it, and enable the active one.\n  5. Health-check the instance.\n  6. Run `nginx -t`. If it fails, remove a listener this run newly created, then exit 1.\n  7. Reload nginx and health-check `127.0.0.1:7079`.\n  The plan's `|| true` on stopping the stray instance was dropped, so a failed stop now fails the install.\n- **Usage text.** It describes the prod template, the instance pair, the nginx files and the prod refusals.\n\n### `engine/uninstall-engine-service.sh`\n- **Prod path.** It sources `engine-upstream.sh`. In prod, any `--service-name` other than `peertube-engine` exits 1. Otherwise it runs the new `uninstall_engine_prod` and exits; the dev path is unchanged.\n- **`uninstall_engine_prod`:**\n  - Dry-run prints a header listing the template, the legacy unit, the listener and the snippet. Outside dry-run it requires root and `systemctl`.\n  - It stops and disables `peertube-engine@7070.service`, `@7071.service` and the legacy `peertube-engine.service`. These lines drop only stderr, not stdout, so their `[dry-run]` lines now show; the existing quirk of hiding them was not copied.\n  - `rm -f` runs in this order: the template and the legacy unit, then the listener, then the snippet and `.bak`.\n  - Outside dry-run: daemon-reload and reset-failed.\n  - If nginx is present: `nginx -t`, and on success `systemctl reload nginx`. If `nginx -t` fails it exits 1 without reloading.\n  - Without nginx, it logs that the check and reload were skipped, and succeeds.\n  - It ends by saying that the deploy lock and any `.service.d` drop-ins are left in place.\n- **Usage text.** It describes the prod removal.\n\n### `scripts/install-service.sh`\n- `install_contour` refuses `--engine-port`/`--engine-host` for the prod contour.\n- `engine_cmd` passes `--host`/`--port` only for dev. They are added at the same position as before, so the dev argv is unchanged.\n- In the usage text, both options are marked dev-only.\n- The prod ingest URL, the echo lines and the collision check are left for Phase 4.\n\n### `engine/watch-engine-logs.sh`\n- `-prod` now follows `UNIT=\"peertube-engine@*\"`; journalctl `-u` takes the glob.\n- The help line was updated to match.\n\n### `engine/engine-upstream.sh`\n- Added `ENGINE_LISTENER_CONF=\"/etc/nginx/conf.d/peertube-engine-internal.conf\"`, which the installer and uninstaller share. See `<unanticipated>`.\n\n### `tests/active/test_installers_dry_run.py`\n- Not created. The Phase 3 checkpoint in `tests/tmp` carries C1 and C2, and this step asked for production code only. Phases 1 and 2 handled their `tests/active` files the same way.\n\n### Verification\n- A throwaway probe loaded the checkpoint module by path and ran every test body in it. All 16 parametrised cases passed:\n  - prod install: no snippet, plus the three accepted snippets;\n  - the seven rejected snippets;\n  - `--port`;\n  - dev, both variants;\n  - uninstall, both variants.\n- I have no delete tool, so `tests/tmp/test_probe_26_p3_impl.py` now holds a single comment line asking for it to be deleted.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nengine/engine-upstream.sh \u2014 added one line, `ENGINE_LISTENER_CONF=/etc/nginx/conf.d/peertube-engine-internal.conf`. The installer and the uninstaller both need the listener path. Phase 2 left it out of the shared library on purpose, as belonging to this phase, but this phase's file list does not name the library.\ntests/tmp/test_probe_26_p3_impl.py \u2014 a throwaway probe. I have no delete tool, so it is now a single comment line asking to be deleted, and it collects no tests.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

    "step_7_implement:4": "<changes>\n### `engine/install-updater-service.sh`\n- Now sources `engine/engine-upstream.sh`, the same way the Engine installer and uninstaller already do. That gives it `UPSTREAM_SNIPPET` (which follows the test override `PEERTUBE_ENGINE_UPSTREAM_SNIPPET`, otherwise `/etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf`), `ENGINE_INSTANCE_BASE` and `ENGINE_INSTANCE_PORTS`.\n- The sudoers rule is built once into `updater_sudoers_rule`. The dry-run preview and the file checked by `visudo -cf` both print that one value, so they cannot drift apart.\n- **Prod:** `updater_exec` gets `--engine-upstream-snippet ${UPSTREAM_SNIPPET}`, placed after the fixed flags and before `${UPDATER_FLAGS}`. It is added in the installer itself, not in the `UPDATER_FLAGS` default, so it survives the `--updater-flags` value that the central installer always passes.\n- **Prod sudoers rule:** exactly `<user> ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: <systemctl> stop peertube-engine@7070, <systemctl> stop peertube-engine@7071, <systemctl> start peertube-engine@7070, <systemctl> start peertube-engine@7071`. It is built from the shared base name and port list, with no `.service` suffix, matching the worker's `systemctl_cmd`. A comment says that `--engine-service-name` no longer affects the prod rule.\n- **Dev:** `ExecStart` and the single-name rule are unchanged.\n- Usage line for prod now names `peertube-engine@7070|7071 (active one from the nginx upstream snippet)`.\n\n### `client/install-client-service.sh`\n- `DEFAULT_PROD_ENGINE_PORT` is now 7079, so the prod default `--engine-url` is `http://127.0.0.1:7079`. A comment says this is the nginx loopback listener. Dev stays on 7171.\n- An explicit `--engine-url` still overrides the default.\n- The `--engine-url` help now states both defaults, and the prod usage example uses 7079.\n\n### `scripts/install-service.sh`\n- Added `PROD_ENGINE_LISTENER_URL=\"http://127.0.0.1:7079\"`. For the prod contour, `engine_ingest_base` is that URL unless `--client-engine-url` is given. Dev keeps `http://${engine_host}:${engine_port}`.\n- Port collision check: in prod it refuses a Client port of 7070, 7071 or 7079. Dev keeps the Engine\u2260Client check.\n- The prod Engine echo line now reads `engine=peertube-engine@7070|7071 via http://127.0.0.1:7079` instead of a host:port the prod Engine no longer uses. Dev's line is unchanged.\n- Phase 3 had left the ingest URL, echo lines and collision check for this phase; they are all done.\n\n### `tests/check-frontend-client-gateway.sh`\n- Added `7079` to both port alternations on the hardcoded-Engine-port guard, as the plan says.\n\n### `tests/active/test_installers_dry_run.py`\n- Not created. The Phase 4 checkpoint in `tests/tmp` carries C1 and C2, and this step asked for production code only. Phase 3 handled the file the same way.\n\n### Verification\n- A throwaway probe loaded the checkpoint by path and ran every test body in it. All 11 cases passed: Client prod, dev and explicit URL; central prod, dev and all; the four updater prod variants (direct or via the central installer, with and without the snippet override); and updater dev.\n- I have no delete tool, so `tests/tmp/test_probe_26_p4_impl.py` is now a single comment line asking to be deleted. It collects no tests.\n\n### Noticed, not changed\n- `tests/run-installers-smoke.sh` is outside this phase's files.\n- `dry_install_prod_engine_port` (line 836) greps the central prod dry-run for `127.0.0.1:7070`. The plan already lists that check as broken since Phase 3.\n- The live-install check at lines 589-595 builds the expected prod ingest base as `http://127.0.0.1:7070`. It will now see 7079.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\ntests/tmp/test_probe_26_p4_impl.py \u2014 throwaway probe; I can't delete files, so it is now one comment line asking to be deleted, and it collects no tests.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "step_8_i1_refactor": "<refactors>\nengine/install-engine-service.sh: the dev unit and the prod template were two copies of the same 17-line unit body that differed only in ExecStart's host and port. They are now one `engine_unit_text <host> <port>` function; dev calls it with `${ENGINE_HOST} ${ENGINE_PORT}` and prod with `127.0.0.1 %i`, for both the dry-run preview and the unit write.\nengine/install-engine-service.sh: removed `DEFAULT_PROD_ENGINE_PORT=7070` and `resolve_default_engine_port`. After Phase 3 only the dev path reaches that code, so `install_engine_service` now defaults `ENGINE_PORT` straight to `DEFAULT_DEV_ENGINE_PORT`.\nengine/install-engine-service.sh: `DEFAULT_PROD_ENGINE_SERVICE` is now `${ENGINE_INSTANCE_BASE}` instead of a second \"peertube-engine\" literal. It has a one-line comment saying why: `install_engine_prod` refuses any other name, so `--print-default-service-name` has to stay equal to the instance base.\nengine/install-updater-service.sh: `updater_exec` was written out once for dev and again in full for prod, and the sudoers rule was built two different ways. Now `updater_exec` is built once with an empty-or-`--engine-upstream-snippet` fragment, and the sudoers rule comes from one stop/start loop over `engine_units`: `(${ENGINE_SERVICE_NAME})` in dev, `peertube-engine@7070 @7071` in prod.\nengine/uninstall-engine-service.sh: the prod default `--service-name` is `${ENGINE_INSTANCE_BASE}` instead of the \"peertube-engine\" literal it is checked against two lines later.\n</refactors>\n\n<left_out>\nengine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py: no change. The new helpers and the stop/start block in `main` are already as small as they can be. The repetition worth removing (`resolve_default_engine_service_name`'s fallbacks, the three `purge_hosts_*` loops) predates this build. That code is also under the `main` source-scan tests, so touching it carries risk with no benefit to this build.\nMoving the prod template path into engine/engine-upstream.sh, so that the installer's `PROD_TEMPLATE_PATH` and the uninstaller's local `template_path` share one definition: this would grow the shared library past what Phases 2 and 3 scoped for it. The gain is one duplicated path.\nengine/install-updater-service.sh `DEFAULT_PROD_ENGINE_SERVICE`: left as a literal. In prod the worker ignores `--service-name` once the snippet is given, so nothing depends on it matching `ENGINE_INSTANCE_BASE`.\nscripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh, scripts/install-service.sh, client/install-client-service.sh, engine/watch-engine-logs.sh, engine/engine-upstream.sh, tests/check-frontend-client-gateway.sh: nothing to consolidate.\nNot run: the real (non-dry-run) unit write now goes through `engine_unit_text \u2026 > path` instead of `printf '%s\\n' \"${content}\" > path`. It is the same printf of the same string, but needs root and systemd, so it was not exercised. A live `install-engine-service.sh` run on the box, or `tests/run-installers-smoke.sh`, would confirm it.\nUnfilled template: the section saying what this pass is measured against reached me as the raw placeholder `{rat_tail_rules}`. As at plan time (plan line 747), I worked from the role's rat-tail convention. No deliberate simplification was added, so no new `rat-tail:` comment was needed.\nProbes left on disk, since I can't delete files: `tests/tmp/test_probe_26_step8_refactor.py`, cut to a single comment line, and `tests/tmp/probe_26_step8_snapshot.json`, cut to a delete-me stub. Both are outside the files I was given and need deleting.\n</left_out>\n\n<needs_fresh_red>\nnone\n</needs_fresh_red>\n\n<observation>\nI saved the --dry-run output of 9 cases before the edits and compared it after, with tmp paths normalised: all byte-identical, exit codes included. The cases were prod install with no snippet, prod install with a 7071 snippet, dev install, `--print-default-service-name`, prod and dev uninstall, uninstall refusing a bad prod name, and prod and dev updater installs.\n</observation>",
    "step_9_triage": "<docs>\n<doc path=\"DEPLOYMENT.md\" update=\"yes\">\nSeveral prod claims are now false. Line 4: prod Engine ports are now the 7070/7071 pair behind `127.0.0.1:7079`. Units table: `peertube-engine.service` is replaced by the template `peertube-engine@.service` with instances `@7070`/`@7071`, and exactly one is enabled (the one the snippet names). The Client row's `--engine-url` is now `http://127.0.0.1:7079`. Day to day: the restart is `sudo scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh --blue-green` (`--timeout 300`, `--warmup 0`, `--drain 30`, `--dry-run`; explain why the drain is 30 s, and note that a 429 counts as not ready). Find the active port with `cat /etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf`. Logs: `journalctl -u 'peertube-engine@*'` or `engine/watch-engine-logs.sh -prod`. Deploy logs are tagged `peertube-engine-deploy`, with a `deploy_id` on each line. A central `--force` restarts the active instance in place.\n\nAdd a migration note: the one-time outage, the Client restart onto 7079, moving any `peertube-engine.service.d/` drop-ins to `peertube-engine@.service.d/` (the installer only warns), and re-running the updater installer.\n\nUpdater timer section: the updater stops/starts the instance the snippet names. Its sudoers rule allows exactly stop/start on `peertube-engine@7070|7071`. It takes `engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock` before the stop, waiting at most 30 minutes, and releases it after the start. A deploy refuses while the updater is active or activating.\n\nTriage: rows 152, 156 and 164-166 name `peertube-engine` and must name the active instance and the deploy. New rows: deploy lock held, updater active, Client preflight refusal (the Client unit lacks `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7079`), `port_in_use_by_foreign_process`, readiness timeout rollback, `nginx -t`/reload/post-switch rollback, `ROLLBACK FAILED` (what state is left behind), `post_switch_failure` (exit 1, traffic already on the new instance), finding the active port, the updater's lock-wait timeout, and an invalid or unreadable snippet (including CRLF, and that it must be 0644).\n\nInstaller examples: prod refuses `--host`/`--port`/`--engine-port`/`--engine-host` and any non-default `--service-name`. Prod install now requires nginx with a `conf.d` include, plus `flock` and `curl`. The uninstaller removes both instances, the template, the legacy unit, the listener, the snippet and `.bak`. It keeps the lock file and drop-ins.\n\n\u00a76: the loopback listener `/etc/nginx/conf.d/peertube-engine-internal.conf` (listen `127.0.0.1:7079` only, `server_tokens off`, its own access log, `client_max_body_size 2m`, headers passed unchanged, `X-Engine-Upstream` response header, nginx default timeouts). Also the snippet as the single source of truth, the `conf.d` include requirement, and that the public site file is unchanged. Firewall: never open 7070, 7071, 7072 or 7079.\n\n\u00a74/\u00a75: manual runs stay on 7070. Warn against `server.py --dev` (it binds 7071) and `scripts/run-services.sh` on a prod host. Note that both instances run during the overlap: roughly double RSS, and both build a random cache.\n\nBehaviour change: with the Engine down, the Client relays nginx's HTML 502. There is no retry and no `ENGINE_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE`, the log line is INFO `status=502`, and a bridge failure reads `engine bridge HTTP 502`.\n\n\u00a77: the debug drop-in goes on `peertube-engine@.service.d/`, followed by a deploy. `seed=` goes to the active port (or 7079), not always 7070.\n\n\u00a78: the prod expectations of `tests/run-installers-smoke.sh` (`PROD_ENGINE_PORT=7070`, ingest base 7070, single unit) are stale.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md\" update=\"yes\">\nExecution Order steps 7, 12 and 14: with `--engine-upstream-snippet`, the worker first takes the deploy lock (non-blocking `flock` polled every 5 s, for up to 30 minutes, opened `O_RDONLY|O_CREAT`; on timeout it fails before any stop). Then it parses the snippet strictly and stops `peertube-engine@<port>`. It starts that same unit in the `finally` and releases the lock after the start, even if the start fails. The lock is held through the merge, popularity and ANN rebuild.\n\nLock Behavior: the deploy lock `engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock` (`--deploy-lock-file`) is separate from the single-run `--lock-file`.\n\nService Stop/Start, line 149: the stale `peertube-browser` becomes the active `peertube-engine@<port>` in prod, and `--service-name` in dev or without the snippet.\n\nImportant Flags: add `--engine-upstream-snippet` and `--deploy-lock-file`.\n\nSystemd Run, line 206: the sudoers rule has exactly four entries, stop/start `peertube-engine@7070` and `@7071` (no `.service` suffix), and prod `ExecStart` passes `--engine-upstream-snippet /etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/README.md\" update=\"no\">\nLine 28 says `seed=` works only on requests sent straight to the Engine. That stays true: the active instance's port and the 7079 listener both reach the Engine with the query unchanged. The sentence names no port or unit, so nothing in it is false. The port detail belongs in DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a77.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DATA_BUILD.md\" update=\"yes\">\nUpgrade order step 4, line 172: \"Restart the Engine\" becomes, in prod, `sudo scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh --blue-green`, run after `whitelist.db` is migrated. Line 268, \"Stop the Engine before running such a build\": in prod, the Engine is whichever `peertube-engine@<port>` the snippet names, and during a deploy both instances are up. Say to stop the active instance (and not to deploy) before a `--recreate-out-db` build.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe \"Service installers\" section lists the operator entry points for the prod contour but not `scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh --blue-green`, which is now the way to restart the prod Engine. Add it with a pointer to DEPLOYMENT.md. The stale root-level `install-service.sh`/`uninstall-service.sh` paths are pre-existing and optional to fix.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nLine 30 says a transport failure answers 502 `ENGINE_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE` and that proxied reads are retried once. In prod, with the Engine down behind the 7079 listener, nginx answers its own HTML 502: the Client relays it with no retry and no `ENGINE_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE` code. Line 34's `engine bridge unavailable` also becomes `engine bridge HTTP 502` in that case. Qualify both for the prod topology. Line 58's manual `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7070` stays valid; add that the prod unit uses `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7079`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/watch-engine-logs.sh\" update=\"no\">\nPhase 3 already updated it. Help line 12 reads `Use peertube-engine@* (both blue/green instances)`, and `-prod` sets `UNIT=\"peertube-engine@*\"`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0002-trusted-proxy-client-address.md\" update=\"yes\">\nDecision item 4 rests the Engine's trust in `X-Client-IP` on \"the Engine binding loopback with the Client backend as its only peer\". In prod, the Engine's peer is now the loopback nginx 7079 listener, which forwards `X-Client-IP` from the Client unchanged. The guarantee holds only because 7079 is loopback-only. This needs an amendment, which is the operator's call (see adr_conflicts). The Consequences line about exposing the Engine should extend to exposing 7079.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0009-engine-blue-green-through-nginx-upstream-snippet.md\" update=\"yes\">\nNew ADR (proposed). It records what was delivered:\n- the 7079 loopback hop between the Client and the Engine;\n- `/etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf` as the only source of truth for the active port;\n- the deploy lock at `engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock`, shared with the updater (made 0644 so the updater can open it read-only);\n- two strict snippet parsers, bash `read_active_port` and Python `parse_upstream_snippet`, tied together by `tests/active/upstream_snippet_cases.json`;\n- phase-driven rollback, with the old instance stopped only after 7079 confirms the target through `X-Engine-Upstream`;\n- the rejected alternatives: a Client restart, `SO_REUSEPORT`, a state file, a two-server upstream, `/run/lock`, `--print-active-port`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0008-similarity-cache-handoff-through-files.md\" update=\"no\">\nContext line 12 already anticipates Engines on 7070 and 7071 from one checkout, and the build relies on that inode-swap handoff unchanged.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"CONTEXT.md\" update=\"yes\">\n\"Active instance\" and \"upstream snippet\" are now domain terms used across DEPLOYMENT.md, UPDATER_WORKER.md and the scripts. Add two glossary entries. Active instance: the `peertube-engine@<port>` the snippet names, the only one taking traffic and enabled for boot. Upstream snippet: the one-server nginx upstream file that decides it (ADR-0009).\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/26-zero-downtime-deploy.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe build is delivered. At harvest, set Status to `enhancement, complete` and move the file to `docs/project/issues/archive/`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/roadmap.md\" update=\"yes\">\nMark 26 as delivered in the runtime-reliability chain (line 157), and in the F4-M7 note (line 117) if it references 26 as pending.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"peertube-browser-service-review.md\" update=\"no\">\nThis is a dated historical review. Its \"no nginx\" and single-unit sudoers statements describe the system as reviewed at the time, not the current state.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/security-audit/run-2/architecture.md\" update=\"no\">\nThis is a dated audit snapshot (run-1 likewise). Its Engine `127.0.0.1:7070` row records the system as audited.\n</doc>\n</docs>\n\n<adr_conflicts>\nADR-0002 (trusted-proxy client address), Decision item 4: the Engine's trust in `X-Client-IP` is justified there by \"the Engine binding loopback with the Client backend as its only peer\". In prod, the Engine's only peer is now the loopback nginx listener on 127.0.0.1:7079, which passes `X-Client-IP` through from the Client unchanged. The trust holds only while 7079 stays loopback-only, so exposing 7079 is now as unsafe as exposing the Engine. The decision still works in practice, but its stated premise is no longer literally true. Amending item 4 and its Consequences is the operator's decision.\n</adr_conflicts>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DEPLOYMENT.md": "<changes>\nI updated DEPLOYMENT.md for the prod blue/green Engine. It now covers the instance pair, the 7079 listener, the deploy command, rollback, the updater lock, the new Triage rows and the installer rules.\n\nI checked every claim against the code: `scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh`, `engine/engine-upstream.sh`, the prod parts of the Engine installer and uninstaller, `scripts/install-service.sh`, the updater installer and `updater-worker.py`, the Client installer, `client/backend/server.py` (how it relays an error and its timeouts) and `watch-engine-logs.sh`.\n\n- **Intro and units table.**\n  - The prod Engine is the pair 7070/7071 reached through `127.0.0.1:7079`. A manual run uses 7070.\n  - `peertube-engine@.service` is a template with `--port %i`, and only the active instance runs and is enabled for boot.\n  - The Client row uses `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7079`.\n  - New row for the two nginx files.\n  - Dev is described as single units on 7171/7172 that are restarted in place.\n- **Day to day.**\n  - Commands: `cat` the snippet to find the active port, `systemctl status 'peertube-engine@*'`, the deploy command, `journalctl -u 'peertube-engine@*'` or `watch-engine-logs.sh -prod`, and `journalctl -t peertube-engine-deploy`.\n  - Warns against restarting a prod instance to load new code.\n- **New \"Blue/green deploy\" subsection.**\n  - Options table: `--timeout` 300, `--warmup` 0, `--drain` 30, `--dry-run`. The 2 s poll stays inside the Engine's `/api/` rate limit, and a 429 counts as not ready. The drain is 30 s because the Client's longest Engine timeout is 20 s (`/api/video/refresh`).\n  - The steps of a run, in order.\n  - Refusals, and rollback for each phase.\n  - `post_switch_failure` / `done result=degraded`, `ROLLBACK FAILED`, signal handling, and the lock being released on any exit.\n  - The log line format with `deploy_id`, and the tag `peertube-engine-deploy`.\n  - Both instances run during the overlap: about twice the memory, and the new one builds its random cache.\n  - The central `--force` restarts the active instance in place.\n- **New \"Moving a host from `peertube-engine.service`\" subsection.**\n  - The one-time outage, the Client moving to 7079, and re-running the updater installer.\n  - Drop-ins must move to `peertube-engine@.service.d/`; the installer only warns about them.\n- **Updater timer.**\n  - In prod the updater stops and starts the active instance, and starts the same one it stopped.\n  - The sudoers rule is exactly stop/start on `@7070` and `@7071`.\n  - The updater takes the deploy lock and waits for it at most 30 minutes. A deploy refuses while the updater runs.\n  - Points to UPDATER_WORKER.md for how the worker reads the snippet and holds the lock.\n- **Triage.**\n  - Existing rows now name `peertube-engine@*`, or the deploy where the fix is to load new code.\n  - New rows:\n    - finding the active port\n    - nginx's HTML 502 with no Engine behind 7079 (points to `client/README.md`)\n    - `lock_held`\n    - `updater_running`\n    - `client_not_on_listener`\n    - `port_in_use_by_foreign_process`\n    - `snippet_invalid`, with the installer and updater wording, CRLF and the 0644 requirement\n    - readiness rollback\n    - rollback at the switch\n    - `ROLLBACK FAILED`\n    - `post_switch_failure`\n    - both instances running outside a deploy\n    - the updater's lock-wait timeout\n  - The dev/prod port row lists the prod ports.\n- **Installer examples.**\n  - Paths changed to `scripts/install-service.sh` and `scripts/uninstall-service.sh`.\n  - I removed the \"convenience wrapper\" block because none of those wrapper scripts exist in the repo.\n  - The dev uninstall example now passes `--keep-updater-state`, which the script requires.\n  - The prod rules: refusals, what the install needs (nginx with the `conf.d` include, `flock`, `curl`), the lock, how the snippet is handled, and the `nginx -t` failure path.\n  - What the uninstaller removes and what it keeps (the lock file and drop-ins).\n- **\u00a74.** No manual Engine, `server.py --dev` or `run-services.sh` on a prod host. A deploy deletes the old instance's random-cache temp file.\n- **\u00a76.** New \"Engine listener on 127.0.0.1:7079\" subsection:\n  - the snippet as the only source of the active port (one line, LF, 0644, `.bak`);\n  - the listener's directives;\n  - headers passed through unchanged, and nginx's default 60 s timeouts;\n  - the `conf.d` include requirement and how to check it;\n  - the public site file is not changed;\n  - why 7079 must stay loopback-only (points to ADR-0002 and ADR-0009).\n  - Firewall: never open 7070, 7071, 7072 or 7079.\n- **\u00a77.** The debug drop-in goes on `peertube-engine@.service`, followed by a deploy; dev keeps its in-place restart. `seed=` goes to 7079 or the active port, or to 7070 for a manual run.\n- **\u00a78.**\n  - `run-installers-smoke.sh`: its prod checks expect a single unit on 7070, so their results on the prod contour are unreliable.\n  - `run-arch-split-smoke.sh`: its Engine port 7072 is the prod Client's port. The old text called its ports unrelated to production.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md": "<changes>\nI updated UPDATER_WORKER.md so it describes how the updater stops and starts the active `peertube-engine@<port>` instance in prod while holding the deploy lock. I checked every claim against `updater-worker.py` and `engine/install-updater-service.sh`.\n\n- **Execution Order**\n  - Step 7: with `--engine-upstream-snippet`, the worker takes the deploy lock first, then reads the snippet and stops the instance it names. If the lock wait times out or the snippet is invalid, the run fails before anything is stopped.\n  - Step 12: the worker starts the same unit it stopped. It releases the deploy lock after that start, even if the start fails.\n  - Step 14: now says \"single-run lock\", so the two locks can't be confused.\n- **Lock Behavior**: new \"Deploy lock\" subsection.\n  - The path is `--deploy-lock-file` (default `engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock`). It is a separate file from `--lock-file`, and `scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh` takes the same lock.\n  - The worker opens it `O_RDONLY|O_CREAT` because root may own it as 0644. It tries a non-blocking `flock` every 5 s for up to 30 minutes, and the timeout message is quoted.\n  - The lock is held from before the stop, through merge, popularity and the ANN rebuild, until after the start.\n  - The deploy side, including its refusal to run while the updater is active, is left to `DEPLOYMENT.md`, with a pointer.\n- **Service Stop/Start Behavior**\n  - Replaced the stale `peertube-browser` unit name.\n  - Prod: the unit is the instance the snippet names. The snippet's format rules are listed, including that CRLF line endings are rejected. The snippet itself is left to `DEPLOYMENT.md` \u00a76, with a pointer.\n  - Dev, or no snippet given: the unit is `--service-name`, defaulting to `peertube-engine-dev` or `peertube-engine`.\n- **Important Flags**: added `--engine-upstream-snippet` and `--deploy-lock-file`.\n- **Systemd Run**\n  - The sudoers rule is exactly stop and start on `peertube-engine@7070` and `@7071` in prod: four entries, no `.service` suffix. Dev keeps the single `--engine-service-name` unit.\n  - The prod `ExecStart` passes `--engine-upstream-snippet /etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DATA_BUILD.md": "<changes>\nDATA_BUILD.md: the schema-upgrade restart and the \"stop the Engine before a `--recreate-out-db` build\" warning now cover the prod blue/green Engine.\n\n- **Upgrade order, step 4.** The step now says that in prod the restart is `sudo bash scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh --blue-green` and points to `DEPLOYMENT.md`. I used `sudo bash \u2026` because that is how the script's own usage text and its root-check error message invoke it.\n- **\u00a75, the `--recreate-out-db` warning.** In prod you stop the active `peertube-engine@<port>` instance, the one the nginx upstream snippet names, and run no blue/green deploy until the build has finished, because a deploy starts a second Engine on the same cache file. How to find the active port is left to `DEPLOYMENT.md`, which this paragraph points to.\n\nI checked these against `scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh` (its `--blue-green` flag and root check) and `engine/engine-upstream.sh` (the snippet path and the 7070/7071 pair).\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:README.md": "<changes>\nREADME.md now has a short \"Restarting the prod Engine\" section with the blue/green deploy command, and the central installer and uninstaller paths are corrected to `scripts/`.\n\n- **New section \"Restarting the prod Engine\"** (directly after \"Service installers\"). It says the prod Engine runs blue/green behind an nginx loopback listener. To run the code currently on disk, you deploy with `sudo bash scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh --blue-green` rather than using `systemctl restart`. For options, rollback, logs and how to find the active instance, it points to `DEPLOYMENT.md` and does not repeat them. I checked the command and the required `--blue-green` flag against the script's header.\n- **Installer paths corrected.** \"Service installers\" and \"Service uninstallers\" pointed to `install-service.sh` and `uninstall-service.sh` in the repo root. Those files don't exist; the scripts are `scripts/install-service.sh` and `scripts/uninstall-service.sh`. I fixed the topology lists and every example command.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:client/README.md": "<changes>\nI updated `client/README.md` for prod, where the Client reaches the Engine through nginx on `127.0.0.1:7079`. I checked each claim against `client/backend/server.py` and `client/install-client-service.sh`.\n\n- **New bullet after the `/api/video/refresh` paragraph.** In prod, a down Engine is not a transport failure. nginx answers with its own 502 and an HTML body. The backend's `HTTPError` branch passes that through like any Engine response: there is no retry, no `ENGINE_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE` code, and an INFO `engine.proxy` record with `status: 502`. The retry and `ENGINE_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE` still apply when the listener itself can't be reached or the request times out, which is the `URLError`/`TimeoutError` branch. For the listener itself, the bullet points to `DEPLOYMENT.md` section 6 rather than repeating it.\n- **Bridge publish bullet.** Added one sentence: in prod, a down Engine behind the `7079` listener reads `engine bridge HTTP 502`. In the code, nginx's 502 arrives as an `HTTPError` in `_publish_to_engine_bridge`.\n- **Run Backend Locally.** The manual `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7070` example is unchanged. A new line under it says the prod unit written by `client/install-client-service.sh --mode prod` uses `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7079` (`DEFAULT_PROD_ENGINE_PORT=7079`), and points to `DEPLOYMENT.md`.\n\nThe \"Engine <operation> failed\" paragraph is unchanged: nginx's 502 still makes `_post_json` return a non-200 status, so the same 502 answer results.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/adr/0002-trusted-proxy-client-address.md": "<changes>\nADR-0002 now says the Engine's trust in `X-Client-IP` rests on the loopback-only 7079 nginx hop as well as the Engine's own loopback bind.\n\n- **Decision item 4:** the trust condition used to be \"the Engine binds loopback and its only peer is the Client backend\". It now says every hop between the Client backend and the Engine must be loopback-only. The Engine binds `127.0.0.1`, and in prod its only peer is the nginx listener on `127.0.0.1:7079`, which forwards the Client's `X-Client-IP` unchanged. The item points to ADR-0009 for the topology. I checked this against `engine_listener_text` in `engine/install-engine-service.sh`: it has only `listen 127.0.0.1:7079` and sets no header except `Host`, so `X-Client-IP` reaches the Engine unchanged. The template's `ExecStart` is `--host 127.0.0.1 --port %i`.\n- **Consequences:** exposing the prod `7079` listener beyond loopback now sits next to exposing the Engine directly, as an unsupported setup that lets a caller spoof `X-Client-IP`.\n- **Your decision needed:** the checklist says amending this ADR is your call. I edited it in place and left Status `accepted` with no \"Amended\" line, so it reads as the current decision. The ADR-0009 reference only holds once that ADR is written in its own turn.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/adr/0009-engine-blue-green-through-nginx-upstream-snippet.md": "<changes>\nCreated ADR-0009 (Status: proposed). It records the Engine blue/green design: the loopback 7079 hop, the snippet as the only source of truth, the shared deploy lock, the two parsers tied to one fixture, phase-driven rollback, and the rejected alternatives.\n\n- **Context:** an in-place restart takes the browser path down. The Client reads `--engine-url` only once, at startup. The updater stops and starts the Engine on its own schedule.\n- **Decision**, six numbered items, each checked against the code:\n  - The 7079 listener in `conf.d`: loopback-only, request headers passed through, `X-Engine-Upstream: $upstream_addr`, no upstream keepalive. Checked in `engine_listener_text` in `install-engine-service.sh`.\n  - The `peertube-engine@.service` template on 7070/7071. Exactly one instance is active and enabled for boot.\n  - The one-server snippet `/etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf` is the only thing that decides the active port.\n  - The deploy lock `engine/server/db/engine-deploy.lock`. It is set to 0644 so the updater can open it read-only. The updater waits up to 30 minutes for it, before its stop and until after its start. A deploy refuses while the updater is running.\n  - `read_active_port` and `parse_upstream_snippet` both reject CRLF. `tests/active/upstream_snippet_cases.json` is the case table both are tested against.\n  - Phase-driven rollback. The old instance is stopped only after 7079 returns 200 with `X-Engine-Upstream` naming the target. The ADR says why a plain 200 is not enough: an old nginx worker can still answer it.\n- **Operations:** how to run and troubleshoot a deploy is left to `DEPLOYMENT.md`, with a pointer, and not restated here.\n- **Alternatives rejected:**\n  - restarting the Client on each flip;\n  - `SO_REUSEPORT` or socket activation;\n  - a state file or a `systemctl` query;\n  - a two-server upstream with `down`/`backup`;\n  - a lock in `/run/lock` (because of `fs.protected_regular`);\n  - `--print-active-port`.\n- **Consequences:**\n  - A change to the snippet format must touch both parsers and the fixture. One shared helper is the upgrade path.\n  - The `X-Client-IP` trust now also depends on 7079 being loopback-only. This points to ADR-0002, which already carries that amendment.\n  - The Client sees nginx's 502 when no Engine is up.\n  - During a deploy, both instances use memory and may each build a random cache.\n  - The deploy refuses when something foreign holds 7071, such as `server.py --dev`.\n  - The dev contour is unchanged.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:CONTEXT.md": "<changes>\nI added two glossary entries to CONTEXT.md: **Active instance** and **Upstream snippet**.\n\n- **Active instance**: the instance the snippet names, either `peertube-engine@7070` or `peertube-engine@7071`. It is the only instance taking traffic and the only one enabled for boot. The other instance stays stopped except during a blue/green deploy, which starts it, moves traffic to it, and only then stops the old one. Points to ADR-0009.\n- **Upstream snippet**: `/etc/nginx/peertube-engine-upstream.conf`, a one-server upstream naming `127.0.0.1:7070` or `127.0.0.1:7071`. The `127.0.0.1:7079` loopback listener sends traffic to it. It is the only thing that decides which port is active, and the deploy script, the Engine installer and the updater all read it. Points to ADR-0009.\n\nI checked the path, the port pair, the 7079 listener port and the one-server rule against `engine/engine-upstream.sh` (`UPSTREAM_SNIPPET`, `ENGINE_INSTANCE_PORTS`, `ENGINE_LISTENER_PORT`, `read_active_port`). I also confirmed that ADR-0009 exists. The deploy steps, the parse rules and the lock are not repeated here; they belong to DEPLOYMENT.md and ADR-0009.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/26-zero-downtime-deploy.md": "<changes>\nIssue 26 is now marked `enhancement, complete` with a Delivered comment. The file is still in `docs/project/issues/` and has to be moved to `archive/` at harvest.\n\n- **Status line:** changed from `enhancement, needs-triage` to `enhancement, complete`.\n- **New `### Delivered` comment under `## Comments`:** it follows the pattern of the archived issue 24. It names the plan `docs/project/plans/19-26-zero-downtime-deploy.md`, with the commit left as `<pending>`. Its bullets mostly point at other documents and don't repeat what they say:\n  - **Command:** `sudo scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh --blue-green`. Options, rollback and log lines are left to `DEPLOYMENT.md`.\n  - **Topology:** the Client reaches the Engine through the loopback listener on 7079, and the upstream snippet alone decides the active port. Points to ADR-0009 for the reasoning and to the two `CONTEXT.md` terms.\n  - **Unit name:** the template is `peertube-engine@.service`, not the `peertube-browser@.service` the proposal gave as an example. Dev keeps its single unit.\n  - **Updater:** it stops and starts the active instance and shares the deploy lock. Points to `UPDATER_WORKER.md`.\n  - **Random cache:** this answers the earlier comment. No per-request inode check was added, and the deploy deletes the old instance's leftover `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` and its `-journal`.\n  - **Live check:** the first two validation items (no 5xx spike over repeated deploys, and a forced rollback) are for the operator to check on the live host. The suite only runs against stub commands.\n- **Checked against the code:** the deploy script (timeout default 300, `X-Engine-Upstream` check, removal of the temp file and its `-journal`) and `updater-worker.py` (`--engine-upstream-snippet`, `--deploy-lock-file`, 30-minute lock wait).\n- **Not done:** the move to `docs/project/issues/archive/`. I have no move or delete tool, and the checklist puts the move at harvest.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/roadmap.md": "<changes>\nI marked issue `26` as delivered in `docs/project/roadmap.md` and added a Delivered entry for it.\n\n- **New \"Delivered\" entry, \"Issue `26`, zero-downtime Engine deploy\".** The entry follows the format of the other entries: one sentence on what was delivered, then pointers. It says the prod Engine runs as `peertube-engine@7070` or `@7071` behind the loopback nginx listener on `127.0.0.1:7079`. It says `scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh --blue-green` starts the other instance, switches the upstream once it is healthy, then drains and stops the old one. It also says the script rolls back on its own if anything fails before the switch is confirmed. Usage detail is left to `DEPLOYMENT.md` (\"Blue/green deploy\"), and the entry links the plan `docs/project/plans/19-26-zero-downtime-deploy.md`. I checked the `--blue-green` and `--drain` options in the script itself.\n- **Runtime-reliability chain (Implementation order).** The line now reads ``22` -> `23` -> `24`/`25` -> `26`; `22`, `23` and `26` are delivered.`\n- **F4-M7 line left as it was.** \"issues `19` to `26`\" only records what the old tracker filed under F4-M7. It does not say any of them are pending, so it needed no change.\n- **Not changed: 24 and 25 stay unmarked.** The roadmap never recorded them as delivered and that was outside this item, so I left them alone. They need a decision:\n  - `25` is archived with `Status: enhancement, complete`.\n  - `24` exists twice. `docs/project/issues/24-similarity-cache-shadow-swap.md` says `ready-for-agent`, and `docs/project/issues/archive/24-similarity-cache-shadow-swap.md` says `complete`.\n  - Once the duplicate is resolved, the chain line and the Delivered list should be updated for 24 and 25.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",

  "requirements": "### Purpose\n\nRestarting the Engine API in place on one port takes the whole browser path down while the new process loads its FAISS index and warms up. That is tens of seconds on a full dataset (DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a74, Triage \"Engine `active` but `/api/health` refuses connections for minutes\"). The browser path is nginx `:80` \u2192 Client backend `127.0.0.1:7072` \u2192 Engine `127.0.0.1:7070` (DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a76; `client/backend/server.py` reads `--engine-url` once at startup, default `http://127.0.0.1:7070`). The build gives the operator one command that restarts the Engine on the code currently on disk (after a `git pull`, a dependency change or an environment change) with no window where the Client cannot reach an Engine. A second Engine starts on the other port of a fixed pair, is health-checked, and gets traffic through an nginx upstream switch; only then is the old one drained and stopped. Failures roll back on their own.\n\n### Decided topology (operator decision)\n\n- The Engine is what gets blue/green. The Client backend is not blue/green and is not restarted by a deploy.\n- nginx is placed between the Client and the Engine through a new loopback-only listener on `127.0.0.1:7079`. It proxies every path to an nginx `upstream` whose single server is the active Engine port (`127.0.0.1:7070` or `127.0.0.1:7071`).\n- The prod Client unit's `--engine-url` becomes `http://127.0.0.1:7079`, permanently. After this one-time change the Client never has to change or restart for an Engine deploy.\n- The public `:80` site config (`/etc/nginx/sites-available/peertube-browser`, DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a76) is not changed by this work. The `7079` listener must bind `127.0.0.1` only and must never be reachable from outside the host; the Engine has no authentication and `/internal/*` accepts writes (DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a76 Firewall).\n\n### Scope\n\n- Prod contour only. The dev contour (`peertube-engine-dev` on 7171, Client dev on 7172) keeps its current single unit and in-place restart, unchanged.\n- Fixed port pair `7070`/`7071` only: no free-port selection, no custom port list, no port options on the deploy script.\n- Out of scope: fetching or updating code (the deploy restarts whatever is on disk), Client backend blue/green, dev-contour blue/green, unit hardening (review findings F1/F3), a per-request random-cache inode check, and `scripts/run-services.sh` (manual/dev runner without nginx; it keeps starting a single Engine on 7070).\n\n### systemd instance template\n\n- A template unit `peertube-engine@.service` replaces `peertube-engine.service` in the prod contour. The name follows the existing `peertube-engine` naming; the issue's `peertube-browser@.service` was only an example. The instance name is the port, so `peertube-engine@7070` and `peertube-engine@7071` can run at the same time.\n- Template content matches today's prod Engine unit (`engine/install-engine-service.sh`): `Type=simple`, same `User=`, `WorkingDirectory=`, `Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, `Environment=ENGINE_INGEST_MODE=bridge`, `EnvironmentFile=-<project>/.env.bridge`, `Restart=on-failure`, `TimeoutStopSec=20`, `WantedBy=multi-user.target`. The one difference is that `ExecStart` takes `--port` from the instance name (`%i`), with `--host 127.0.0.1`.\n- The prod Engine installer (`engine/install-engine-service.sh --mode prod`, also reached through `scripts/install-service.sh`) installs the template instead of the single unit. On an existing install it migrates: it stops and disables the old `peertube-engine.service`, removes its unit file, then starts and enables one instance, `peertube-engine@7070`, and writes the snippet pointing at 7070. Re-running the installer is idempotent; it must not flip or restart a healthy active instance just because it is re-run without `--force`.\n- Exactly one instance is enabled for boot: the one the snippet names. A deploy enables the new instance and disables the old one.\n- The Engine uninstaller (`engine/uninstall-engine-service.sh --mode prod`, and `scripts/uninstall-service.sh`) stops, disables and removes both instances and the template, and removes the nginx snippet and the 7079 listener config that the installer wrote. Afterwards nginx must still pass `nginx -t` and keep serving the public site.\n- `--help` and `--dry-run` keep working on all installer and uninstaller entrypoints. `tests/run-installers-smoke.sh --dry-run-only` relies on both.\n\n### nginx: single source snippet and internal listener\n\n- One snippet file is the single source of truth for which Engine port is active. It contains only the upstream definition, one server line: `127.0.0.1:7070` or `127.0.0.1:7071`. Nothing else (no state file, no systemctl query) decides which port is active.\n- A loopback-only server block listens on `127.0.0.1:7079`, includes or references that upstream, and proxies every path to it.\n- The listener passes request headers through unchanged. In particular `X-Request-ID` from the Client must reach the Engine as sent: it is neither stripped nor replaced. `X-Client-IP` and `X-Bridge-Token` must also arrive unchanged, because the Engine's rate limiter keys on `X-Client-IP` (DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a76) and `/internal/*` authenticates on `X-Bridge-Token` (\u00a73b). This keeps the work compatible with `X-Request-ID` forwarding from issue `20-request-lifecycle-logs`, which is not delivered yet.\n- Proxy timeouts on the listener must not cut off legitimate long Engine requests (up-next FAISS searches are not bounded by the 5 s statement deadline, DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a74 \"Up-next logs and load\"). Keep nginx defaults or set them at least as generous.\n- Setup of the snippet, the listener and the Client's `--engine-url` change is scripted, with no manual nginx edits: done by the prod install path (Engine and Client installers or the central `scripts/install-service.sh`). Setup validates with `nginx -t` before reloading.\n- The prod Client installer (`client/install-client-service.sh --mode prod`) writes `--engine-url http://127.0.0.1:7079` by default. Dev keeps `http://127.0.0.1:7171`.\n\n### Deploy command\n\n- New script `scripts/deploy-bluegreen.sh`. It operates on the repository root the same way `scripts/run-services.sh` resolves it.\n- It requires the explicit `--blue-green` flag. Without it the script prints usage and exits non-zero, with no side effects.\n- It supports `--help` and `--dry-run`. Dry-run prints the detected active port, the target port, and every action it would take, without starting, stopping, writing or reloading anything.\n- Options: a readiness timeout in seconds (default 300, matching `run-services.sh` `HEALTH_TIMEOUT`); an optional warm-up wait in seconds after the first healthy answer (default 0); a drain wait in seconds between the switch and stopping the old instance (default long enough for in-flight requests to finish; design picks the value and documents it).\n- It runs as root (via sudo), like the installers, because it calls `systemctl` and `nginx`. It fails fast with a clear message otherwise, except in `--dry-run`.\n- One command does the whole deploy. No step needs a manual `systemctl` call or nginx edit.\n\n### Deploy flow\n\n1. Acquire an exclusive non-blocking lock (flock on a fixed lock file). If another deploy holds it, exit non-zero at once with a message, touching nothing.\n2. Refuse to start (non-zero, message) while the prod updater service (`peertube-updater.service`) is active, since it stops and starts the Engine itself.\n3. Read the active port from the snippet. If the snippet is missing or names anything other than 7070/7071, stop with an error and touch nothing. The target port is the other one of the pair.\n4. If the target instance is already running (leftover from an interrupted deploy), stop it first. A leftover is restarted, never reused, so the deploy always runs freshly started code.\n5. Start `peertube-engine@<target>`.\n6. Readiness: poll `http://127.0.0.1:<target>/api/health` until it returns HTTP 200 or the readiness timeout expires. The poll interval must stay well inside the Engine's `/api/` rate limit, because `/api/health` sits behind `_rate_limit_check`. Then wait the optional warm-up time and check health once more.\n7. Switch: keep a copy of the current snippet, write the new snippet atomically (temp file plus rename) naming the target port, run `nginx -t`, then reload nginx.\n8. Post-switch check: `http://127.0.0.1:7079/api/health` returns 200.\n9. Wait the drain period, then stop `peertube-engine@<old>` with `systemctl stop` (SIGTERM; the Engine shuts down gracefully), enable the new instance and disable the old one.\n10. Remove the old instance's leftover `engine/server/db/random-cache.tmp.<old MainPID>.db` if one exists. The PID is recorded before the stop. A stop during a background cache build leaves this file, and it is safe to delete (issue comment; DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a74).\n11. Release the lock and exit 0.\n\n### Automatic rollback\n\n- Readiness failure (timeout, or the target unit fails or exits): stop the new instance; the snippet and nginx are untouched and the old instance keeps serving. Exit non-zero.\n- `nginx -t` failure, reload failure, or post-switch check failure: restore the previous snippet, run `nginx -t`, reload nginx, stop the new instance. The old instance keeps serving. Exit non-zero.\n- The old instance is never stopped before the switch has been verified (step 8).\n- After the switch is verified, failures (stopping the old instance, enable/disable, temp-file cleanup) are logged and make the exit code non-zero, but do not roll back the switch, because traffic is already on the new instance.\n- A failure inside rollback itself (for example the restore's `nginx -t` fails) is logged loudly with the state left behind, and exits non-zero.\n- The lock is released on every exit path, including signals.\n\n### Idempotency\n\n- Re-running after a successful deploy deploys again: it flips to the other port. Re-running after an interrupted or failed deploy converges, because the snippet is the only source of truth and a leftover target instance is restarted, not reused.\n- A deploy never leaves both instances serving through nginx: the upstream names exactly one server at every moment.\n\n### Updater compatibility\n\n- `engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py` currently stops and starts one fixed unit name (`--service-name`, default `peertube-engine`). In prod it must stop and start the active instance instead: the one the snippet names when the updater reaches its stop step. It must start the same instance it stopped.\n- The updater's sudoers rule (`engine/install-updater-service.sh`, `/etc/sudoers.d/peertube-updater-systemctl`) must allow exactly `stop` and `start` on `peertube-engine@7070` and `peertube-engine@7071`, nothing broader.\n- A deploy and the updater's Engine stop/start window must not overlap in either direction. The deploy refuses while the updater is active (flow step 2), and the updater must not stop/start an Engine while a deploy holds the lock; design picks the mechanism.\n- Dev updater behaviour is unchanged.\n\n### Random cache and similarity cache during the overlap\n\n- Both instances building `random-cache.db` during the overlap (each with its own `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db`) is accepted, as is the extra CPU while both run.\n- Readiness does not wait for a random-cache build. `/api/health` does not report it, and the Engine serves the random feed from `whitelist.db` until its build finishes (DEPLOYMENT.md \u00a74). The optional warm-up wait is the operator's control for this.\n- No per-request inode check is added. Only one instance takes traffic at a time, and the old instance is stopped after the drain, so a sibling holding an old `random-cache.db` inode only lasts for the overlap.\n- The similarity cache needs nothing new. Running Engines already reopen a swapped `similarity-cache.db` on their next cache access (DEPLOYMENT.md \"The updater timer\").\n\n### Logging\n\n- Every deploy has a deploy id, unique per run (for example UTC timestamp plus PID). Every log line carries it.\n- Logged at minimum: deploy id, old port, new port, the switch time (when the reload succeeded), the health result (HTTP status and seconds waited, for readiness and for the post-switch check), the drain and stop outcome, and on any rollback the rollback reason and the step it happened at.\n- Lines go to stdout and to journald through `logger` with a fixed tag, matching `log_lifecycle` in the installers (`logger -t peertube-service-lifecycle`, or a deploy-specific tag; design picks).\n\n### Documentation\n\n- `DEPLOYMENT.md` is updated: the units table (template instances replace `peertube-engine.service` in prod); \"Day to day\" (deploy command instead of `systemctl restart peertube-engine`, and how to find the active instance); the nginx section (the 7079 listener, the snippet, and that 7079 must stay loopback-only; Firewall says never open 7070, 7071, 7072 or 7079); the updater section (it stops/starts the active instance); Triage rows for deploy lock held, readiness timeout, nginx validation failure and rollback, and finding the active port; the Client `--engine-url` in prod; and \u00a77's note that `seed=` goes to the Engine directly, which now means the active port, not always 7070.\n- Every other doc that names `peertube-engine.service` for prod, or 7070 as the only prod Engine port, is brought in line (`README.md`, `engine/server/README.md`, `engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md`, as the impact inventory finds them).\n\n### Validation\n\n- Automated tests run without root, systemd or a real nginx, using stub `systemctl`, `nginx`, `curl` and `logger` injected through PATH or environment, the way `updater-worker.py` takes `--systemctl-bin` and `--skip-systemctl`. They cover: a normal flip 7070\u21927071 and back 7071\u21927070 (snippet contents, start/stop/enable/disable calls in order, old stopped only after the switch); readiness-timeout rollback (new stopped, snippet unchanged, old untouched, non-zero exit); `nginx -t` failure rollback; reload failure rollback; post-switch probe failure rollback (previous snippet restored); lock contention (second run exits non-zero without side effects); refusal without `--blue-green`; refusal while the updater is active; leftover target instance restarted; missing or invalid snippet refused; leftover `random-cache.tmp.<old pid>.db` removed; required log fields present, including the rollback reason.\n- The updater's active-instance resolution and the installer's template/sudoers output are covered by tests or by dry-run contract checks in `tests/run-installers-smoke.sh --dry-run-only`.\n- Operator validation on the live host, not automated: repeated deploys show no 5xx spike in the nginx access log for the public site, and a forced failure (for example a readiness timeout of 1 s, or a deliberately broken snippet) exercises rollback with the old instance still serving.\n\n### Baseline suite state\n\nPre-build suite exited 0 (baseline variant: false). Paths: active tests `tests/active`, working `tests/tmp`, plans `docs/project/plans`, archive `tests/archive`, delete-me `delete_me`, record `tests/last_test_validation.json`, output `tests/last_test_output.txt`, project dir `/home/enduser/code/PeerTube-browser`.",
